goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:37 — Browsers using the legacy box fallback cannot distribute horizontal space through this auto margin, so header controls lose their former right alignment.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real compatibility issue. The diff shows `.panel` changing from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto` with `@include order(3)`. The flexbox mixins in mixins.scss include legacy prefixes like `-webkit-box` and `-moz-box` for older browsers. However, `margin-left: auto` for auto-distribution of space only works in modern flexbox, not in the legacy `-webkit-box` or `-moz-box` display modes. Browsers using these legacy fallbacks would not properly right-align the panel element since auto margins don't work the same way in the old box model. This is a legitimate cross-browser compatibility bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:264 — The description now shrink-wraps without flex-grow, pulling its right-floated action buttons beside short descriptions instead of retaining alignment at the row's right edge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `.small-action` gets `@include flexbox()` and `@include align-items(center)` added, making it a flex container. The `.small-action-desc` child has its padding changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, but no `flex-grow` property is added. In a flex container, without `flex-grow: 1` or similar, the `.small-action-desc` element will only take up as much width as its content requires (shrink-wrap behavior). This could cause layout issues where action buttons that were previously right-aligned via the full-width description would now appear immediately after short description text instead of at the right edge.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:102 — The flexbox mixin emits `-moz-box`, but the companion alignment mixin omits `-moz-box-align`, making the advertised legacy fallback incomplete.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the `flexbox()` mixin at line 97-103 includes `-moz-box` as a display value for Firefox legacy support. However, the `align-items()` mixin at lines 117-123 only includes `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items` - it's missing `-moz-box-align` which would be the corresponding property for the `-moz-box` display mode. This is an inconsistency in the legacy browser fallback implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:263 — No regression test covers the direct-child action button after flexbox makes its float-based right alignment ineffective.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a 'direct-child action button' that uses float-based right alignment that would be broken by flexbox. Looking at the diff for topic-post.scss, the changes are to .small-action (adding flexbox), .small-action-desc (changing padding), and nested p elements (removing margins). There's no evidence in the diff of any action button with float-based right alignment being affected. The finding appears to reference code/behavior not shown in the diff.
